title: Sunrise on the Reaping Roars to a $110 Million Opening — Haymitch's Hunger Games Is Here
excerpt: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened Friday with $21.25 million in previews and a projected $110 million weekend — Lionsgate's biggest debut in 11 years.
content:
Panem is back — and the box office is already calling it. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened in theaters Friday, November 20, and the numbers from its first night point to the biggest opening Lionsgate has had in more than a decade.

The sixth film in the franchise earned $21.25 million in Thursday previews and early-access screenings, according to Deadline, the second-best preview total in franchise history behind only 2013's Catching Fire at $25.2 million. Friday is estimated at $51 million including previews, putting the film on course for a projected $110 million domestic opening weekend. Through Friday, the global total stood near $76 million.

The film is playing in 4,018 theaters across North America — the widest screen count in Lionsgate history — and it would be the studio's first $100 million-plus opening since The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2 in 2015.

Haymitch's story, at last

Sunrise on the Reaping adapts Suzanne Collins' 2025 novel of the same name, which sold more than 1.5 million copies in its first week of publication. The story returns to the 50th Hunger Games — the Second Quarter Quell, set about 24 years before the original trilogy — and follows a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, the character Woody Harrelson played as a hardened, older mentor to Katniss Everdeen.

Joseph Zada, a 20-year-old Australian actor, plays the young Haymitch. Whitney Peak plays his girlfriend, Lenore Dove; Mckenna Grace plays fellow District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner; Ben Wang plays Wyatt Callow; and Molly McCann plays Louella McCoy. The Capitol side of the cast is stacked: Ralph Fiennes as President Coriolanus Snow, Jesse Plemons as Plutarch Heavensbee, Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket, Kieran Culkin as Caesar Flickerman, and Glenn Close as District 12 escort Drusilla Sickle. Francis Lawrence directs his fifth film in the series, from a screenplay by Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie. It runs 2 hours and 38 minutes.

The Quarter Quell twist doubles the tributes, so District 12 sends four young people into the arena instead of two — and Haymitch, who survives to become Katniss's mentor, has to find a way to fight the Capitol's game from inside it.

What the reviews say

Critics are split. The film sits at 74% on Rotten Tomatoes from 101 reviews, the third-best critics' score in the franchise behind Catching Fire and the original film. Audiences are far more enthusiastic: the audience score is 95%, the best in franchise history, ahead of Catching Fire at 89%.

The weekend's other wide opener, the Stallone biopic I Play Rocky, is estimated at about $10 million — a distant second.

En México: Amanecer en la cosecha

The film opened the same weekend in Mexican theaters as Los Juegos del Hambre: Amanecer en la Cosecha, in dubbed and subtitled versions, as part of a global rollout projected at more than $200 million for the opening weekend.

What it means

Analysis: The franchise's bet is that the audience never really left Panem — it just needed a reason to come back. The preview numbers, more than triple the last prequel's, say the reason was Haymitch: the one character whose past every fan of the original films wanted to see. The split between critics and audiences is the other half of the story. A 74% critics' score is respectable, but a 95% audience score is the number that fills seats on a holiday weekend, and Lionsgate is counting on Thanksgiving week word of mouth to carry the film past its opening. Whether the prequel can hold the way the originals did will be decided next weekend — but for now, the arena is full again.
